top.lede: Dance, drawing, karate, music, abacus and spoken English, all at one address on Diamond Harbour Road. One fee card, one pickup point, and no running across Behala between tuitions.
top.p: First class is free. Admissions open all year. Batches of 12 or fewer.

classes.h2: Pick one class or mix two
classes.lede: Every class has its own trained teacher, its own room and its own colour on the timetable. Children who take two classes get a discount on the second.

photo.alt: A young boy dancing in traditional dress beside an Odissi dancer at a festival

classes.p: Rabindra Nritya, folk and Bollywood. Children perform twice a year at our annual show and at the para Pujo stage.

photo2.alt: A girl colouring a drawing with crayons at a table

classes.p2: Pencil, crayon, poster colour and watercolour. We prepare children for school art exams and district drawing competitions.

photo3.alt: Two young students sparring in protective gear at a taekwondo match

classes.p3: Shotokan karate with belt gradings every six months. Good for confidence, focus and fitness. Uniform available at the centre.

photo4.alt: A teacher in a blue saree playing harmonium while four children sing along

classes.p4: Rabindrasangeet and light vocal, with harmonium and keyboard basics. Small groups so every child gets to sing alone too.

photo5.alt: A girl writing sums in a lined notebook with a pencil

classes.p5: Eight levels of abacus and mental arithmetic. Children do sums faster than a calculator by Level 4 and sit for national competitions.

photo6.alt: Schoolgirls in white uniforms listening in a classroom

classes.p6: Speaking practice, not grammar drills. Stories, show-and-tell, short speeches. Children from Bengali-medium schools pick up fast.

timetable.lede: All weekday classes run after 3.30 pm so children come straight from school. Weekend classes are in the morning. Slide the table sideways on a phone.
timetable.sr: Weekly class timetable by day and time
timetable.p: Centre is closed on Wednesday mornings and on the main Pujo days. Timetable changes are sent on the parents' WhatsApp group a week ahead.

photo.alt: A teacher at a smart board in front of a class of students in maroon uniforms

about.h2: Started in a two-room flat in 2016
about.lede: Mitali Sen taught dance from her front room in Behala for nine years before taking the ground floor at 14/1 Diamond Harbour Road. Parents kept asking if someone could also teach drawing, then karate, then English. So we added one class at a time, hiring teachers we would send our own children to.
about.lede2: Today there are three air-conditioned rooms, nine teachers and a small waiting area with a water filter where parents sit and chat. We know every child by name.

join.h2: Four steps, no forms to print
join.h3: The first class is always free
join.p: Try dance on Monday and karate on Wednesday if you like. Decide after.

items.p: Send the child's age and the class you have in mind on WhatsApp. We reply within the day with the free slots.
The child sits in one full class. Parents can watch from the waiting area. No payment that day.
Fees are monthly, paid by UPI or cash at the desk by the 10th. There is a one-time admission fee of ₹300.
Timetable changes, holidays, show dates and photos from class come on the WhatsApp group.

section-7.h2: Every child goes on stage once a year
section-7.p: Our annual show is in December at the Behala Blind School auditorium. Dance, music and karate students perform. Drawing students' work is hung in the lobby. Parents come, grandparents come, nobody sits at the back.

items.p: My daughter does dance and drawing on alternate days, so I drop her at 4 and pick her up at 6 from the same gate. For a working mother that is the whole point.
Our son would not speak a word of English in front of people. After eight months of the Sunday batch he gave a two-minute speech at his school. We were not expecting that.

fees.lede: Monthly fees, no yearly lock-in. Leave with a week's notice.
fees.feenote: Karate uniform ₹650 and drawing kit ₹350 are bought once, at cost. Belt grading and competition entry fees are paid to the organising body, not to us.
fees.summary: Can my child start in the middle of the month?
fees.p: Yes. We charge only for the classes left in that month and start full fees from the next month.
fees.summary2: What if we miss a class?
fees.p2: Tell us a day before and the child can attend the same class in another batch that week. We do not refund missed classes.
fees.summary3: Can parents sit in the class?
fees.p3: For the free trial, yes. After that parents wait in the waiting area so the children settle. You can watch through the glass panel any time.
fees.p4: A staff member sits at the gate from 3.30 to 8.30 pm. Children are handed over only to the person named on the admission form, and we have CCTV in the corridor and waiting area.
fees.p5: Karate belts come from the state association. Abacus levels come with a certificate from our affiliating body. Dance, music and drawing students get our own annual certificate and perform on stage.

items.td: Second class for the same child
